description.p: Brevier fetches a page, reduces it to Markdown on your own machine, and renders it in the typography you chose — not the one the site shipped. There is no JavaScript engine and no site CSS. What survives is the text.
It also reads Markdown documentation straight out of git repositories: point it at a GitHub or GitLab project and it shows the README, the entry points into the docs, and the files of any directory.

ul.li: One measure, one scale, one paper colour on every site, light or dark
Fonts that travel with the program, so the page cannot pick its own
A shelf with the page's table of contents, the site's own menu, and the project's documentation
Tabs that survive closing the window, history, bookmarks, and page search
Images off by one switch: after JavaScript is gone, the image decoder is the one serious attack surface left
One key to hand the page to your usual browser when a site needs more than text

description.p: Known limits, stated rather than hidden: no JavaScript means single-page sites do not work, there are no forms or logins, and screen readers are supported on Linux only.

description.p: Early build, shared for testing: the window, the repository mode, tabs, history, bookmarks and saving are there; packaged builds and screen-reader support beyond Linux are not.
